assumptions: A willing installer can lawfully authorize the workflow and execute an adequate controller-processor agreement without granting the founder rights to its customers or records.
The product remains advisory and evidentiary unless an external institution explicitly recognizes it; it does not claim to guarantee DSO, subsidy, or warranty acceptance.
Relevant installation and successor-program activity continues at enough annual volume to test a narrow Polish beachhead despite slower microinstallation growth.
AI and automation can handle most document extraction and deterministic rule checks, while qualified humans review exceptions and legal or security requirements.
The founder can obtain the first pilot through a voluntary family-firm relationship but must win unrelated installers through ordinary commercial selling.
The proposed pricing, unit volume, gross margin, and founder-wealth path are treated as hypotheses rather than evidence.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots with several unrelated installers showing sustained crew completion, a material reduction in correction work or collection delay, repeat purchases at the proposed price, and fully loaded contribution margin after support and manual review; a signed distributor, platform, DSO, program, or OEM integration that makes the check a recognized workflow gate would raise the ceiling further.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The idea targets a real coordination failure: renewable-installation evidence is fragmented across subsidy, DSO, handover, and warranty packets, and official evidence shows unusually frequent correction or completion requests. A cross-brand pre-handover check is a coherent wedge, but it is an incremental workflow insight rather than a proprietary mechanism, and the passport cannot replace official forms or external acceptance decisions.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: More than 40% of assessed Mój Prąd 6.0 applications being returned and rejection for a missing OSD certificate establish meaningful paperwork failure. The packet does not establish how much of the loss falls on installers, whether it delays their cash, or whether they will pay repeatedly for validation. The 145.53 PLN net adjacent filing offer supplies a plausible price anchor, but that service performs more of the administrative outcome and has no verified sales evidence.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-install pricing matches a recurring operational event, prepaid bundles could produce good cash conversion, and software-assisted exception handling could support attractive margins. However, every decisive economic input remains unmeasured, including CAC, retention, support load, exception-review time, and contribution margin. Charging 120-250 PLN plus a monthly fee is vulnerable when an adjacent provider advertises completed OSD filing at 145.53 PLN net, so the proposed 65-80% margin and scale path are plausible hypotheses rather than a strong economic case.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Small Polish photovoltaic, battery, and heat-pump installers are a specific, reachable beachhead with repeated documentation events. Poland's 1.6 million-plus installed microinstallation base and continuing successor programs support sector relevance, but installed base is not annual transaction volume, target-account count is unknown, and microinstallation growth had already decelerated materially.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A focused Polish, cross-brand rules layer could serve small installers better than manufacturer-specific tools. Yet Reonic already bundles configurable checklists, mobile and offline capture, signatures, documentation, and PDF handover reports; OEMs control parts of device commissioning; and service providers can complete filings. With no recognized acceptance status or exclusive workflow position, a dominant segment position is not yet structurally supported.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful installation evidence workflow could expand across batteries, heat pumps, multiple DSOs, subsidy programs, warranty documentation, distributors, and eventually nearby EU markets. Those adjacencies share capture and rules infrastructure, although each new institution, program, equipment family, or jurisdiction also adds maintenance and integration complexity.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Public rules, templates, OCR, checklists, and report generation are reproducible, while the proposed installer agreement is nonexclusive, revocable, and replaceable. The hypothesized exception-data advantage depends on lawful retention, scale, and predictive value that are all unproven, and broader installer platforms and OEMs may accumulate better proprietary workflow data.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Cross-brand rule maintenance and one neutral audit trail could be more convenient than scattered manual files or separate OEM apps. No evidence shows a large improvement in acceptance rate, installer labor, payment speed, or warranty recovery, and the current offer appears narrower than a competitor that handles actual filing and highly overlapping with a bundled installer platform.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Successor household-energy programs, changing document templates, required photos, and automated photo-integrity checks create ongoing demand for current and structured evidence. Conversely, the original Mój Prąd intake is closed, rules are unstable, and installation growth has slowed, so timing creates both need and continuous maintenance risk rather than a clear temporary opening.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The founder has a credible route to request one low-cost, separately consented pilot through the family operating relationship, and a small-installer B2B sale is compatible with targeted founder-led outreach. There is no signed pilot, no authority to mandate use, no evidence that family access generalizes, and distributor, software-partner, conversion, CAC, and payback routes remain hypothetical.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow rules, capture, OCR, and exception-review MVP is technically compatible with the founder's data-science skills, AI leverage, 45,000 PLN proposed budget, and part-time limit. The harder work is operational: maintaining changing rules, earning crew compliance, securing controller-processor contracts, protecting sensitive records, and supporting exceptions without becoming an on-call document service. These risks are material but testable without large upfront capital.

highest_value_structural_change: Move from a generic evidence passport to an outcome-linked completion rail that owns preparation and submission for a narrowly chosen institution or program, is embedded as the installer's mandatory pre-handover checkpoint, and charges per accepted or correction-free packet; this would make the economic benefit clearer and differentiate it from a useful PDF checklist.
main_structural_strength: A frequent per-install operational event can support usage-based repeat revenue, the first pilot is unusually accessible, and the software-led rules-and-exception workflow fits the founder's skills, capital, and part-time constraints.
primary_score_limiter: The venture does not control the acceptance outcome and has not demonstrated an advantage strong enough to displace bundled workflows or outcome-completing filing services at an attractive recurring price.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Reonic already offers nearly the same mobile checklist, photo, signature, documentation, and PDF-handover workflow, while an adjacent Polish provider advertises completed OSD filing for 145.53 PLN net and external institutions retain all acceptance authority. Together, these facts undermine both differentiation and the proposed validation-only price point.
